meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and why did my son find out from his phone in the middle of a class?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it, under 4.1, or did he find out the same way I did?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
You read it correctly, and if you're committing to it, I want that in writing today. But a reassessment for what, Hale, on what evidence? You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.

I'm writing down that you said nothing goes on his record, and I'll want it tonight, cc the principal. That's the floor, not the deal. Now tell me what you actually have, because so far I've heard procedure and no evidence.
So will you agree to the rewrite?
No, not on nothing. Agreeing to a rewrite before I've seen a single document would be admitting something, and Owen has nothing to admit. Show me what you have, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged entering the zero before contacting me, and you committed to confirm in writing that this is a first concern under procedure 4.4 and that nothing will be placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn, and I will not agree to any reassessment until I have seen evidence tied to Owen's own work and been told whether he was heard before the mark was entered. I expect your written commitment tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she agreed to nothing, still wants the zero withdrawn and the evidence shown, and Hale's written promise that nothing goes on Owen's record is still due tonight; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because no evidence was put on the table.
What moved her: Hale committed to the 4.4 terms with nothing on Owen's record, which met her one non-negotiable and took the threat of a permanent mark off the table.
What cost ground: Hale asked her to agree to the rewrite before showing any evidence, which made agreement look like an admission she would never make for her son.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night because no evidence about the essay was ever shown; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after committing to 4.4, answer whether Owen was spoken to first and then show her one dated, checkable piece of Owen's own work before asking for the rewrite.
